profile.summary: BiRNA-BERT is an RNA language model that turns an RNA sequence into embeddings for downstream prediction tasks. It can read a sequence either one nucleotide at a time, for fine-grained tasks such as secondary structure prediction, or as compressed byte-pair tokens, so that long RNAs can be processed without cutting them short. It is a 117M-parameter transformer encoder trained on about 36 million non-coding RNA sequences.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper abstract; model card opening paragraph

summary_quotes.text: we introduce BiRNA-BERT, a 117M-parameter Transformer encoder trained on 36 million non-coding RNA sequences

At its core is an adaptive dual-tokenization framework that combines nucleotide-level (NUC) encoding for fine-grained structural tasks with byte-pair encoding (BPE) for efficient long-sequence processing.
BiRNA-BERT is a BERT-style transformer encoder model that generates embeddings for RNA sequences.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: BiRNA-BERT is a BERT-style transformer encoder trained with the MosaicBERT framework. It uses ALiBi relative positional encoding instead of fixed position embeddings, which lets it handle sequences longer than those seen in training. Its main idea is dual tokenisation: the same model is trained by masked language modelling on both byte-pair encoding (BPE) tokens, with a vocabulary of 4096, and single-nucleotide (NUC) tokens. BPE compresses long sequences so they fit in memory, while nucleotide tokens keep the per-base detail needed for tasks such as secondary structure prediction. With the released tokenizer, an unspaced sequence is split into BPE tokens and a space-separated sequence into nucleotide tokens.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results (first paragraph), Methods (tokenisation); model card: Usage

quotes.text: The architecture integrates ALiBi relative positional encoding to maintain attention across long sequences, and an adaptive tokenization strategy that applies Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) for long sequences and nucleotide-level (NUC) tokenization for short sequences.
BiRNA-BERT was trained using the MosaicBERT framework
char_embed = mysterybert(**tokenizer("A G C T A C G T A C G T", return_tensors="pt"))

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The main checkpoint is buetnlpbio/birna-bert, used with the tokenizer buetnlpbio/birna-tokenizer. The paper also trained BPE-Only-BERT and NUC-Only-BERT as controls, and the buetnlpbio account lists bpe-only-rna-bert and nuc-only-rna-bert. The README warns that the current version is substantially updated and suggests re-analysing data processed with earlier versions. The README's own embedding example loads a different model name, Lancelot53/birnabert-2ep, while the model card loads buetnlpbio/birna-bert; the sources do not explain the difference. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision (this page read revision 35bceaf6) and say whether BPE or nucleotide tokenisation was used.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: RNA language model (masked language model) that produces embeddings for RNA sequences.
facts.source_locator: Model card: opening paragraph; paper Methods

quotes.text: BiRNA-BERT is a BERT-style transformer encoder model that generates embeddings for RNA sequences.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: BERT-style transformer encoder built with MosaicBERT, with ALiBi relative positional encoding. config.json: 12 layers, hidden size 768, intermediate size 3072, 12 attention heads, vocabulary 4096.

quotes.text: BiRNA-BERT was trained using the MosaicBERT framework
The architecture integrates ALiBi relative positional encoding

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: RNA sequences as text. Unspaced input is tokenised into BPE tokens; space-separated input into single-nucleotide tokens. The card examples use the letters A, G, C and T.

quotes.text: tokenizer("A G C T A C G T A C G T", return_tensors="pt")

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Per-token embeddings: one per BPE token for sequence-level use, or one per nucleotide for nucleotide-level tasks, plus CLS and SEP tokens. The card replaces the masked-language-model head with an identity layer to read them out.

quotes.text: it can generate both granular nucleotide-level embeddings and efficient sequence-level embeddings (using BPE)

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 117M (BiRNA-BERT), as stated in the paper abstract. No count is given for the BPE-only and nucleotide-only control models.

quotes.text: we introduce BiRNA-BERT, a 117M-parameter Transformer encoder trained on 36 million non-coding RNA sequences

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: About 36 million non-coding RNA sequences from RNAcentral, 26.42 billion nucleotides in total, trained for two epochs.

quotes.text: The dataset from RNAcentral encompasses approximately 36 million RNA sequences, collectively containing 26.42 billion nucleotides.
Pretraining was performed on 26.42 billion nucleotides from RNAcentral, using the MosaicML framework on eight NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPUs over two epochs.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: buetnlpbio/birna-bert (main model) with buetnlpbio/birna-tokenizer; control models bpe-only-rna-bert and nuc-only-rna-bert. The same account also lists DNA models (bidna-bert, bpe-only-dna-bert, nuc-only-dna-bert), which are not described in the sources read. The README notes the current version is substantially updated from earlier ones.

facts.value: Not reported. The paper names RNAcentral as the data source but does not give the release or download date in the passages read.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: No fixed limit: ALiBi lets the model take sequences longer than its training length, and BPE shortens long inputs. config.json sets alibi_starting_size and max_position_embeddings to 128; the card says the config default is 1024 and shows raising alibi_starting_size to 2048. The sources do not explain the 128 versus 1024 difference.

strengths.text: One model gives both nucleotide-level embeddings, for structure tasks, and compressed BPE embeddings, for long sequences, so only one set of weights needs to be in memory.

quotes.text: we argue that a single model training on both is memory-efficient since only one set of weights needs to be on memory and can process longer sequences and larger batch sizes.

strengths.text: Long sequences need not be truncated: BPE shortens them by about six-fold and ALiBi extrapolates beyond the training length, according to the authors.

quotes.text: enabling it to process arbitrarily long sequences without truncation
while simultaneously reducing the token count by 6-fold

strengths.text: The model is small and cheap to train by the authors' account: 117M parameters, pretrained on eight consumer RTX 4090 GPUs.

quotes.text: on eight NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPUs over two epochs

limitations.text: No licence is stated for the code or the weights, so terms of reuse are unclear.
BPE tokens lose information: the authors estimate each BPE token holds about 75% of the information of nucleotide tokens, and BPE cannot be used for nucleotide-level tasks.
limitations.source_locator: Paper: Information theoretic analysis; Nucleotide-level task

quotes.text: BPE tokens preserve approximately 75% of the information contained within the NUC tokens
It is worth mentioning here that the dual tokenization scheme of BiRNA-BERT is not applicable in the case of such nucleotide-level tasks, as BPE compression will cause the model to lose information

run_guide.summary: Install the listed Python packages and compute BPE and nucleotide embeddings for one short sequence with the published checkpoint.
prerequisites: Python with the packages in requirements.txt: torch, transformers, tqdm, numpy, pandas, einops, triton.
Internet access to download buetnlpbio/birna-bert and buetnlpbio/birna-tokenizer from Hugging Face. The weights are not gated.
Loading runs remote code from the Hugging Face repository (trust_remote_code=True).
No licence is stated for code or weights. GPU type and memory for inference are not stated.

steps.title: Compute embeddings
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
import transformers
from transformers import AutoModelForMaskedLM, AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("buetnlpbio/birna-tokenizer")

config = transformers.BertConfig.from_pretrained("buetnlpbio/birna-bert")
mysterybert = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained("buetnlpbio/birna-bert",config=config,trust_remote_code=True)
mysterybert.cls = torch.nn.Identity()

# To get sequence embeddings
seq_embed = mysterybert(**tokenizer("AGCTACGTACGT", return_tensors="pt"))
print(seq_embed.logits.shape) # CLS + 4 BPE token embeddings + SEP

# To get nucleotide embeddings
char_embed = mysterybert(**tokenizer("A G C T A C G T A C G T", return_tensors="pt")) 
print(char_embed.logits.shape) # CLS + 12 nucleotide token embeddings + SEP
PY
steps.explanation: The model card's embedding example, unchanged, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It loads the published checkpoint and prints the shape of the BPE and nucleotide embeddings.

quotes.text: print(seq_embed.logits.shape) # CLS + 4 BPE token embeddings + SEP
print(char_embed.logits.shape) # CLS + 12 nucleotide token embeddings + SEP

outputs: Two tensor shapes: one for CLS, 4 BPE token embeddings and SEP, and one for CLS, 12 nucleotide token embeddings and SEP, as the card's comments describe.
